items.prompt: Explain how management can improve satisfaction for Omi’s experienced workers. Omi Print staff say they have no chance to solve production problems although they understand the equipment. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Job satisfaction is enjoyment derived from feeling that you have done a good job. Managers can support it through meaningful work, recognition, suitable responsibility, opportunities to develop and respectful relationships. Fair pay and safe conditions matter too, but improving them does not automatically create achievement from monotonous tasks. Identify the workers’ actual concerns before choosing a response. Job enrichment adds challenge or responsibility, whereas merely adding similar repetitive tasks may increase workload without satisfaction. Genuine responsibility requires appropriate authority and support. Consultation can reveal practical improvements and make staff feel heard, but raising expectations without a credible response can undermine trust. Letting a supported team investigate recurring faults can provide achievement and responsibility. Management should respond to its proposals and acknowledge results rather than calling extra repetitive output a satisfaction programme.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Job satisfaction is enjoyment derived from feeling that you have done a good job.

items.prompt: Explain why Teya needs cooperation and shared delivery responsibility. At Teya Furniture, sales staff consult production before promising delivery dates and both teams review whether customers receive complete orders. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Cooperation means people working together towards a shared objective. Joint responsibility means accepting a shared obligation for an outcome while retaining clear individual duties. Cooperation can reduce incompatible decisions, share knowledge and help departments solve problems together. It does not change the legal ownership of the enterprise. Shared responsibility also does not mean nobody is accountable: define contributions, authority and reporting so that an omission is not passed between departments. Different interests remain, and cooperation requires communication and fair treatment rather than an instruction to agree with management about everything. Shared information helps avoid impossible promises and supports reliable delivery. Sales remains responsible for accurate commitments and production for its schedule; joint responsibility links their efforts instead of removing those duties.
marking_guidance: Starting point: Cooperation means people working together towards a shared objective.

items.canonical_answer: A shop steward can gather members’ concerns, explain union information, represent workers in discussions, help members use agreed grievance arrangements and keep them informed about negotiations. A credible steward can help clarify misunderstanding before a disagreement grows, while recognising when support from wider union officials is needed. Effective links require listening to members as well as speaking to management. A verified shared list can focus discussion and reduce rumours. Reporting the response back to members closes the communication loop rather than leaving workers uncertain about what was agreed.

These definitions describe organisational arrangements, not a claim that a particular requirement is currently lawful or enforceable in every place. Use the facts of the arrangement rather than treating the terms as interchangeable. The first describes a single union agreement; the second supplies the defining closed-shop condition. The first alone does not prove compulsory membership.

Explain the rule, hear evidence and review the allocation rather than assuming the dispute is caused by workers disliking work.

items.prompt: Explain how parties could address Nela’s shift-payment disagreement. Nela Foods’ management and worker representatives disagree over shift payments. They can share evidence and discuss proposals before considering an agreed independent ruling. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Clear communication, consultation, agreed responsibilities and fair procedures can help avoid unnecessary conflict. When relations break down, negotiation lets parties discuss differences and seek a mutually acceptable agreement. Collective bargaining is negotiation by unions and employers over pay and conditions; the syllabus glossary uses negotiation and collective bargaining as two names for the same process between management and workforce representatives. Arbitration involves an independent third party hearing both sides and giving a ruling. Begin by identifying the issue and parties, gathering relevant facts and using the agreed discussion arrangements. If direct agreement fails, an appropriate third-party route may help. Which method suits depends on the dispute. Negotiation gives the parties a chance to reach their own settlement. Arbitration shifts the determination to a third party under the chosen arrangement, so it should not be described as merely another informal chat.

items.prompt: Explain how arbitration differs from continued direct negotiation in this dispute. An employer and union cannot agree and accept an independent person to hear evidence and give a ruling. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Arbitration means listening to both sides in an industrial dispute, trade union and management, and then giving a ruling of what the arbitrator thinks is fair to both sides. Whether the ruling binds both sides depends on what they agreed beforehand. The third party’s determination identifies arbitration. Merely chairing a conversation without making a ruling would not be the same function.

items.canonical_answer: For this syllabus comparison, dismissal concerns the employer ending an individual’s employment for a reason connected to that person, such as stated misconduct or inability to perform, whereas redundancy concerns a role no longer being needed. A redundant worker need not have performed badly: a department can close or technology can remove the job. In wider legal usage, termination categories and protections require precise rules, so the comparison does not establish that any particular termination is lawful. Identify the reason in the case rather than calling every job loss poor performance. The removed packing role illustrates redundancy; the individual conduct case illustrates the dismissal distinction. The worker’s personal performance is not the reason the packing role disappears.
marking_guidance: Difference: For this syllabus comparison, dismissal concerns the employer ending an individual’s employment for a reason connected to that person, such as stated misconduct or inability to perform, whereas redundancy concerns a role no longer being needed.

items.prompt: Evaluate whether a quality circle suits Tano’s defect problem better than a broad worker council. Tano Print has a recurring sealing defect on one line. Operators know the process and can investigate it during scheduled problem-solving time. [8]
items.canonical_answer: A quality circle is a small group meeting to identify and suggest solutions to work or quality problems. A worker council provides a representative forum for wider workplace matters. Democratic leadership consults workers and considers their views when making decisions. They differ in purpose, membership and scope. Choose a quality circle for a specific recurring technical problem when the workers have useful knowledge and time to investigate. A representative council can suit changes affecting many departments, while direct democratic discussion can suit a manageable team. Participation takes time and needs relevant information. It should not delay an urgent safety response or create a false promise that every suggestion must be accepted. A quality circle suits the focused defect better than creating a broad council solely for that issue. Management should evaluate and respond to proposals. For an organisation-wide change to shifts, a representative council would provide broader coverage.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: A quality circle is a small group meeting to identify and suggest solutions to work or quality problems.

items.prompt: Explain how Rena’s quality circle could improve its sealing process. Rena Packaging’s line operators examine why seals fail and propose a change after reviewing the pattern. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A quality circle is a small group of workers meeting regularly to identify, investigate and suggest solutions to work or quality problems. It draws on practical knowledge and can support recognition and satisfaction. Members need relevant information, time and a management response. It is not automatically a decision-making board or a forum for every employment issue. A proposal still needs assessment against cost, safety and other constraints. Their focused practical investigation fits a quality circle. Management should evaluate the proposal and explain its response instead of leaving the group with no feedback.

items.prompt: Explain how a representative council could address Onda’s cross-department change. Onda Stores has several departments affected by new opening hours and seeks representatives from each to discuss the change. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A worker council is a representative forum through which workers’ views on wider workplace matters can be discussed with management. Representation helps include different groups when consulting everyone directly is impractical. Clear selection, scope, information and reporting back matter to credibility. It differs from a small quality circle focused on a specific work problem. Consultation does not by itself mean workers own the business or have a veto over every decision. A council can gather varied concerns and communicate proposals across departments. Representatives must report back so participation does not end with the few people at the table.

items.prompt: Explain how an employers’ association can support Eno’s management. Eno Metals joins a workshop-employers’ association to obtain advice on managing staffing changes and discuss shared industry concerns. [6]
items.canonical_answer: An employers’ association is a group of employers joining together to provide benefits to its members. It can represent employer interests, share information, offer advice, support training (such as off-the-job courses for members’ staff, or guidance for on-the-job training) and contribute to bargaining or discussions affecting an industry. It is distinct from a trade union representing workers, although both may participate in industrial-relations discussions. Membership can pool expertise that one small employer cannot easily obtain alone; subscriptions and differing member interests can limit its appeal. An association does not become the employer of every member’s workers merely by providing advice. The association supports employers, while the employees’ union represents workers. Advice may improve preparation but does not guarantee that every dispute will be resolved in the employer’s favour.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: An employers’ association is a group of employers joining together to provide benefits to its members.

Nara Packaging plans a new shift arrangement across production, sales and dispatch. Workers feel excluded and believe the allocation is unfair. Management can allow two weeks for discussion and is comparing a worker council with a small quality circle originally formed to study sealing defects.

Choose the council with clear scope and feedback to staff; retain the circle for its focused quality task.

items.prompt:
Nara Packaging plans a new shift arrangement across production, sales and dispatch. Workers feel excluded and believe the allocation is unfair. Management can allow two weeks for discussion and is comparing a worker council with a small quality circle originally formed to study sealing defects.

a Explain how unclear participation and perceived unfairness could cause conflict at Nara, and how an appropriate forum could help. [8]
b Evaluate whether the benefits of participation outweigh its costs before Nara’s shift change. [12]
items.canonical_answer: a Exclusion can make workers believe management ignores practical needs, while an unexplained allocation encourages suspicion of unfairness. This can weaken cooperation and obstruct the change. Representatives from each affected department can gather concrete concerns, compare the staffing constraints and report responses back. Participation must precede the final decision and include a credible response; a forum used only to announce it may deepen distrust. b Worker input can reveal scheduling conflicts, improve fairness and support acceptance. Consultation takes time and representatives can disagree, but two weeks are available and the issue affects the whole operation. Use a representative council with a clear timetable, decision scope and feedback process. The benefit outweighs the manageable delay because the present conflict concerns exclusion and fairness. Management should explain any rejected proposal rather than promise that every demand will be accepted; urgent action without time for discussion would require a different balance.
